correctness.rationale: The one-sided Lévy quantile derivative has global lower bound greater than 2.1619 while the perturbation derivative has modulus at most 1.36035, proving a smooth monotone distinct quantile law. On N_p>=k and N_q<ell both rank-selected sums agree exactly. Coupling and union bounds give the full finite-n TV inequality. Conditional binomial counting on N_p=k-1 and k<=N_q<ell supplies a matching lower large-deviation exponent for the specified coupling disagreement, with relative-entropy rates 0.0216008541 and 0.0257320925. Hoeffding at Q(.55) proves sample-level distinguishability. A standard-library checker passed 24,271 supplementary assertions; finite verification is not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The paper recommends two separated rank bands as a discriminating goodness-of-fit statistic. The theorem identifies an explicit infinite-dimensional mechanism for false reassurance: smooth non-Lévy alternatives change a visible central part of the distribution, are consistently detectable by full-sample empirical CDF tests, yet induce exponential total-variation closeness of the exact published statistic under all rejection rules. The finite-n bound (1.51e-6 at n=500) and exact KL coupling exponent quantify practical sample-size insensitivity; this is a structural detection boundary for a motivated test rather than a bare normalization or algebraic identity. The conclusion is not extended to other ensemble/combined tests.
